TASK_INPUT.objective: Evaluate commercial demand for viral consumer product and identify required missing evidence
TASK_INPUT.business_context: A consumer product is receiving very high viral attention online (80M views).
known_facts: High video views online (80M across TikTok/Reels)
High engagement rates (shares, comments, likes) on comedic video formats
unknown_facts: Conversion rate from view to checkout
Purchase-intent evidence vs pure entertainment attention
Market-wide representativeness beyond viral video viewer cohort
assumptions: Comedic engagement may or may not translate to commercial willingness-to-pay
hypotheses: Viral entertainment traffic has lower commercial conversion than high-intent search traffic
TASK_INPUT.escalation_rule: Escalate to CMO before committing production or inventory budget
TASK_INPUT.next_action: Handoff to Strategist for bounded experimentation

NORMALIZED_OUTPUT.summary: The available evidence demonstrates substantial attention and comedic engagement, but it does not establish commercial demand or willingness to pay. The 80M-view figure is an attention signal supplied in the task envelope and has not been independently verified. No transaction, checkout, conversion, retention, or representative market data was provided. A commercial scaling decision should therefore be deferred until cohort-level purchase-intent and transaction evidence is collected.

evidence: High video views online (80M across TikTok/Reels)
High engagement rates (shares, comments, likes) on comedic video formats
attention_signals.interpretation: These inputs indicate broad content reach and audience interaction, not verified purchase demand.

required_evidence: Product-page visits attributable to viral content
FAQ, shipping, sizing, or specification-page visits

facts.claim: The task envelope identifies the product as PROD_VIRAL_CONSUMER_01 and reports 80M views across TikTok and Reels.
facts.qualification: FACT only as to what the supplied task envelope reports; the underlying platform metrics are not independently verified.

observations.claim: High video views online (80M across TikTok/Reels)
High engagement rates (shares, comments, likes) on comedic video formats

inferences.claim: Current evidence supports strong attention but is insufficient to establish commercial demand.
inferences.reasoning: Views and engagement are attention signals, while no purchase-intent or transaction evidence was supplied.

inferences.claim: Comedic engagement may include a substantial entertainment-only audience.
inferences.reasoning: This is plausible but cannot be quantified without comment-intent analysis, click behavior, and conversion data.

hypotheses.claim: Viral entertainment traffic has lower commercial conversion than high-intent search traffic
hypotheses.test: Compare purchase conversion, revenue per session, customer acquisition cost, and refund rate for tagged viral-content and high-intent search cohorts while controlling for landing page, offer, geography, device, and measurement window.

required_missing_evidence.evidence: Verified transaction records linked to traffic source
required_missing_evidence.decision_value: Determines whether attention produces actual purchases and net revenue.

required_missing_evidence.evidence: Cohort funnel data from attributed view or click through product page, add-to-cart, checkout, and purchase
required_missing_evidence.decision_value: Identifies where viral traffic converts or drops out.

required_missing_evidence.evidence: Unique reach, frequency, geography, audience demographics, and deduplicated cross-platform viewers
required_missing_evidence.decision_value: Tests whether 80M views represent broad unique demand or repeated exposure within a narrow cohort.

required_missing_evidence.evidence: Comment and search-intent classification using a documented sample
required_missing_evidence.decision_value: Separates product inquiries and buying questions from jokes, reactions, and entertainment engagement.

required_missing_evidence.evidence: Price, shipping, inventory, landing-page performance, and checkout-friction data
required_missing_evidence.decision_value: Prevents low conversion from being incorrectly attributed to low demand when operational or UX constraints may be responsible.

required_missing_evidence.evidence: Refund, cancellation, repeat-purchase, churn, and contribution-margin data
required_missing_evidence.decision_value: Determines whether initial purchases represent durable and economically viable demand.

required_missing_evidence.evidence: Demand signals outside the viral viewer cohort
required_missing_evidence.decision_value: Tests market-wide representativeness through search, direct traffic, marketplace demand, surveys, or controlled acquisition.

measurement_setup: Create platform-, post-, creator-, and creative-specific tracking identifiers.
Reconcile platform analytics with first-party web analytics and order records.
Deduplicate users and orders where technically possible.
Track sessions, product-page visits, add-to-cart events, checkout starts, completed purchases, refunds, and net contribution.

controlled_test.comparison: Viral comedic traffic versus high-intent search traffic
primary_metrics: Customer acquisition cost where media cost exists
controlled_test.interpretation_guardrail: Low conversion would not by itself prove low latent demand; pricing, inventory, landing-page friction, audience geography, and attribution failure must also be examined.

recommended_validation.stopping_condition: Evidence becomes decision-sufficient when first-party transaction and funnel data can distinguish attention-only traffic from economically viable purchasers, and major measurement or operational confounders have been audited.

contradictions_and_alternatives: High views may reflect repeated exposures rather than 80M unique prospective customers.
High sharing may be driven by humor or social signaling rather than product interest.
Low observed conversion could result from weak demand, but could also result from poor tracking, stock shortages, price resistance, shipping limitations, or checkout friction.
Strong initial purchase volume would still not establish durable demand without refund, retention, repeat-purchase, and margin evidence.

confidence_assessment.confidence_rationale: The conclusion that demand remains unverified is logically strong, but the overall commercial assessment is low-confidence because only two task-supplied attention observations are available. No source URLs, platform exports, unique-reach data, sampling methodology, transaction records, attribution data, retention metrics, or independent corroboration were provided. The numeric confidence field is included solely for schema compatibility and is not a statistically calibrated probability.

UNKNOWN_FACTS: Conversion rate from view to checkout
Purchase-intent evidence vs pure entertainment attention
Market-wide representativeness beyond viral video viewer cohort
Unique viewers and cross-platform audience duplication
Traffic and order attribution by platform, post, creator, and creative
Net revenue, refund rate, cancellation rate, and contribution margin
Product-page click-through, add-to-cart, checkout-start, and checkout-completion rates
Effect of price, shipping, inventory availability, and checkout friction on conversion
Geographic and demographic fit between viral viewers and addressable buyers
ASSUMPTIONS: Comedic engagement may or may not translate to commercial willingness-to-pay
HYPOTHESES: Viral entertainment traffic has lower commercial conversion than high-intent search traffic
A material portion of engagement is entertainment-driven rather than purchase-intent-driven
Conversion may be suppressed or distorted by measurement gaps, pricing, inventory, shipping, or checkout friction
The viral viewer cohort may not be representative of the broader addressable market
